text: The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and all it contains.
Whoever prays the Fajr prayer is under the protection of Allah.
Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, and the Quran at dawn — indeed, the dawn recitation is witnessed.
Whoever prays both the cool prayers enters Paradise.
Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at specified times.
The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most regular ones, even if they are small.
And seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, it is difficult except for the humbly submissive to Allah.
Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing.
He who observes Fajr and 'Isha prayers in congregation, it is as if he has prayed the whole night.
The angels of the night and the angels of the day come together at Fajr and 'Asr.
Verily, with hardship comes ease.
O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
The first thing a person will be held accountable for on the Day of Judgment is prayer.
Prayer is the pillar of religion.
Every night when one-third of it remains, our Lord — Blessed and High — descends to the lowest heaven and says: Is there anyone calling upon Me, that I may respond to him?
Whoever wakes from sleep and says 'La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu al-mulk wa lahu al-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir' — his sins will be forgiven.
By the dawn and the ten nights — indeed in that is an oath for one who thinks.
The believer who sleeps should not feel secure from tests; even sleep is an opportunity squandered or seized.
Guard strictly your prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah devoutly obedient.
Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear.
The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer.
Blessed is He who made the morning appear — every morning is a new beginning before your Lord.
When the muezzin calls at Fajr, know that Allah is calling the whole earth to rise.
Fajr is not just a prayer; it is a declaration that the day belongs to Allah before it belongs to anything else.
By the morning brightness, and the night when it covers with darkness — your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He detested you.
Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you.
The pen has been lifted and the pages have dried — everything is written. But how you meet what is written is your choice.
Do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
The night has a sound of its own — those who stand in it hear what the sleeping cannot.
Say: My prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.
Waking for Fajr is waking to choose your Lord over your sleep. That choice, made every morning, shapes your soul.
Allah said: When My servant comes closer to Me through voluntary acts, I love him. And when I love him, I become his hearing, his sight, his hand.
Do not let the world distract you from what is required of you. The dunya is a bridge — cross it, do not build on it.
Indeed, after every hardship comes ease. After every hardship comes ease.
The person who sleeps through Fajr has let Shaytan urinate in his ear.
O mankind, worship your Lord, who created you and those before you, that you may become righteous.
Every morning the earth receives mercy. Will you be there to receive it with her?
Your Lord says: Call upon Me; I will respond to you.
He who truly loves something, his heart is with it even when he sleeps.
And remember your Lord when you forget and say: Perhaps my Lord will guide me to what is nearer than this to right conduct.
The Prophet ﷺ was the most consistent of people in performing his deeds. When he did something, he would do it regularly.
Sleep is a mercy; Fajr is the gift on the other side of that mercy. Take both.
Indeed, in the alternation of the night and the day and what Allah has created in the heavens and the earth are signs for a people who fear Allah.
No fatigue, nor disease, nor sorrow, nor sadness, nor hurt, nor distress befalls a Muslim — not even a thorn prick — except that Allah expiates some of his sins.
The morning is a mercy and a test in the same breath. How you begin it speaks to where you place your heart.
Successful indeed are the believers — those who are humble in their prayers.
Never is a believer stricken with discomfort, hardship, illness, grief, or even a worry that troubles him, except that Allah expiates his sins.
The one who stands in Fajr is not just waking for himself. He wakes for everyone who depends on his character, his conscience, his care.
Whoever reads Ayat al-Kursi after every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except death.
And it is He who makes the night a cover for you and sleep a rest, and makes the day a resurrection.
One prayer offered in congregation is worth twenty-seven times more than a prayer offered alone.
Fajr arrives the same time every day — it is you who must decide whether to arrive with it.
Shall I tell you the key to Paradise? It is: La ilaha illa Allah.
Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers, in a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability.
Whoever prays Fajr, let him remember: he has seen what angels celebrated all night.
Be in this world as though you are a stranger or a wayfarer.
O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice.
The eye of the dawn does not open twice. Once this moment passes, it belongs to yesterday. Greet it.
There is no day that passes except that an angel calls: O son of Adam, I am a new day, and I am a witness over your deeds in me.

Take advantage of five before five: your youth before your old age, your health before your sickness, your wealth before your poverty, your free time before your busyness, and your life before your death.
There is a comfort in waking before the world — a stillness that reminds you who you are before the noise begins.
And He is with you wherever you are. And Allah, of what you do, is Seeing.
Whoever prays Fajr in congregation, then sits and remembers Allah until the sun rises, then prays two rak'ahs — he will have a reward like that of Hajj and Umrah.
Every breath you take on the way to prayer is a sadaqa. Every step is counted.
Consistency in small acts is how the character is built. One Fajr, then another, then another — and suddenly you are someone who does not miss.
So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
The Prophet ﷺ said: When any one of you sleeps, the Shaytan ties three knots. Pray Fajr and the knots are undone.
There is a light that comes before the sun — it belongs to those who woke for Allah before it arrived.
O Allah, bless my ummah in their early morning hours.
The night asks nothing of you except that you return to your Lord before it ends.
Certainly will the believers have succeeded: those who, when afflicted with calamity, say Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.
Make things easy, do not make them difficult; give glad tidings and do not drive people away.
Allah looks to your hearts and your deeds, not to your faces and your wealth.
Fajr is proof. Proof that you showed up when no one was watching, when nothing was owed, when the only reason was Allah.
The best rows for men are the first rows, and the worst are the last rows.
